children: U.S. STOCKS RISE WITH TECH OUTPERFORMING, OIL DIPS AGAIN
Wall Street indexes are higher, with the Nasdaq composite
up more than 1.5% and the S&P 500
up slightly more than 1%, outpacing gains in the Dow
, with U.S. equities bouncing back from Wednesday's selloff after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates as expected and flagged more to come as it battles stubborn inflation.

In recent months strategists have questioned whether Fed Chair Kevin Warsh would raise rates close to November's midterm elections. But Goldman Sachs said it now expects the Fed to hike interest rates again in October with the argument that "it is most natural to deliver hikes that the FOMC presented today as supporting “a timelier return” to the 2% target at consecutive meetings."

After some choppy trading on Wednesday, investors appeared to be comfortable with the prospect of more hikes, as they saw Wednesday's policy tightening as something the Fed needed to do for credibility, especially as U.S. President Donald Trump has put public pressure on the central bank to cut rates.

Citing doubts about Warsh's credibility after the Fed held rates steady in July, Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, said in a research note that "doubts were dispelled" on Wednesday.
Investors were likely encouraged by the prospect of a second straight day of declines for oil futures on easing supply worries. However, both U.S. crude
and Brent
, the international benchmark, are still trading above $100.
One sector standing out from the crowd is the S&P 500 technology index
, up more than 2%. Within tech, chip stocks are the clear outperformers with the PHLX semiconductor index
up 3%.
On the other end of the spectrum, energy
, down 0.5%, and financial services
, down 0.4%, are among groups on the losing side.
Here is your snapshot from 10:31 a.m. ET (1431 GMT):
Main US indexes rise; Nasdaq and S&P 500 both up >1%
Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers, energy weakest group
Euro STOXX 600 index advances ~0.9%
Dollar down; US crude falls ~2%; bitcoin up ~1%; gold gains >2%
US 10-year Treasury yield falls to ~4.95%
